## TL;DR

The requested CLI pass found two cases where invalid input looked successful. `list` treated an unknown status as a request for the whole board, and `upgrade` silently treated an invalid release channel as stable. Both now fail early with actionable choices and a nonzero exit code. Regression tests cover each behavior. The other requested commands displayed help successfully and returned usage errors with exit code 1 when required arguments were omitted.

## Work and rationale

I read the task specification and inspected the command help registry, dispatcher, task command handlers, and the restart and upgrade argument handling. The main behavioral issue in `list` was in the implementation rather than its help text: the column selector fell back to all visible columns whenever the supplied status was not recognized. That fallback erased the distinction between “show everything” and “the user typed a typo.” I added an explicit validation step at the start of `cmdList`, before the server path or local board lookup. The message lists accepted columns and prints the existing usage form, and `process.exitCode` is set to 1. The local test calls the command with an invalid value and asserts all three parts of the response.

The second issue was in upgrade’s channel parser. It returned `null` both when no channel was requested and when `--channel` had no value, or an unsupported value. Since `null` is the stable channel, invalid requests could be reported as successful on package-manager or source installs, where no network fetch would later expose the mistake. I added a validation guard before install detection so missing and unsupported channel values consistently produce an error and code 1 regardless of installation type. The tests cover an unsupported value and a missing value. This keeps the supported choices aligned with the registered help text: beta, canary, and rc.

The user-facing findings and limits are in `docs/qa/2026-11-cli-usability.md`. The QA record distinguishes checks performed locally from server-backed behavior that requires a live server. No real board writes were used for the probes.

## Approaches tried

I first reviewed the source surfaces that define command usage and the handlers that process arguments, then built the current worktree so execution would reflect the changed source. I ran the requested help and bad-input cases from a disposable repository under `/tmp`, invoking the compiled CLI directly. This avoids relying on the `repoos` executable linked to a different checkout. The scratch run confirmed all eleven help paths exited 0. Missing positional arguments for the commands where they are required returned exit 1 and printed usage. The invalid list filter and invalid upgrade channel exposed the two defects fixed here.

I also added focused automated tests instead of relying only on terminal output. The list test ensures validation happens before any board or server lookup by using an input that must return immediately. The upgrade test calls the command directly with invalid inputs and checks that the message explains accepted values and the process exit code is nonzero.

## Challenges and blockers

The worktree’s default `repoos` command is linked to RepoOS and resolves board commands from the main checkout when invoked inside a linked task worktree. During the first exploratory command batch, a list command therefore printed the main board. It was read-only and no files or task metadata were changed. After recognizing the resolution behavior, I moved all follow-up probes to the compiled entry point from a disposable repository. I did not run commands that create, update, start, move, review, or complete real tasks.

The missing-argument checks do not establish how commands behave against valid task IDs when no control-plane server is running. The acceptance scope here is help text, parser failures, actionable errors, and exit codes. Server-backed success and failure flows would require a live server and are not claimed in the QA findings.

## Key learnings

A forgiving fallback can hide a typo even when the command’s help is accurate. `list` now validates the filter at the boundary, before doing I/O. Parsers should also distinguish an omitted optional value from an invalid value: for `upgrade`, using `null` for both meanings silently selected the stable channel. Validating `--channel` before installation detection makes the outcome independent of how RepoOS was installed.

The CLI QA harness should invoke the task worktree’s compiled entry point from a dedicated scratch repository. That is important for read-only commands too, because some board reads intentionally resolve to the main checkout. The QA document records this operational limitation and the exact coverage so future passes can extend it without treating a narrow parser check as an exhaustive integration run.
